St. James through New York is $750\u2013$800. Don't wander through there broke.","private_thought":"Built 4/4/4 orange ($300). Cash left $358. Rents $750/$750/$800. p2 liquidity cap ~$199+$300 house sales+$200 Boardwalk=$699, so any orange hit bankrupts them and I inherit reds+Boardwalk. They can't reach orange for ~2 of their turns (on Penn Ave). Next roll from CC (space 2) only hits cheap spots unless p3 houses pink: max realistic Virginia 3h is $300 (they have $705, can't reach 4h). $358 covers that and Chance-to-Illinois ($300) or repairs on 12 houses ($300). Do not unmortgage SL ($110 for $25 rent). Do not trade TN or give p2 cash. After this, end turn unless build fails."}}
message.reasoning:
I need to make a decision in this Monopoly turn.

I have $658 and three houses on the Orange monopoly. SHORT_LINE is mortgaged. I hold one Get Out of Jail Free card. Opponent p2 has a red monopoly with partial houses and $199. Opponent p3 has light blue and pink monopolies with no houses and $705.

Opponent p4 has only $46 and is on WATER_WORKS. I will not unmortgage SHORT_LINE. I plan to add a fourth house to the Orange monopoly next turn if I still have over $550 after moving.

I am weighing whether to end my turn or build a fourth house on Orange. Four houses would cost $300 and raise rent to $750–$800, but I need the cash buffer for upcoming landings on hostile properties.

I am on space 2, the Community Chest after passing GO. My next roll could land me on Income Tax, Reading RR, or Oriental. I need to assess whether p4's Oriental is part of a light purple monopoly.

I mapped the rent costs for every possible landing from space 2. Most spaces are safe: Vermont, Connecticut, St Charles, States, and Virginia all carry doubled rent because p3 owns the full light blue or pink monopolies with no houses built yet. Only Oriental would cost a base rent of $2. The remaining rolls hit Chance, Electric, Jail, and Income Tax.

Turn order is p2, p3, p4, then p1. p3 will finish building before I roll again.

p3 can build heavily with $705. Pink houses cost $100 each and light blue $50. From space 2, I land on pink properties on rolls 9, 11, and 12. That is about a 19% chance. Light blue properties are hit on rolls 6 and 7. That is about a 31% chance. p3 might prioritize pink for higher rent or light blue to block me.

p3 can max out the pink monopoly at seven houses for $700, leaving only five dollars. Even three houses there would cost $700 and raise rent to $270–$300, which is still manageable with my $658. Light blue houses cost only about $100 each. The real danger is if p3 stacks all its money on one property I might land on.

Even if p3 maxed out the pink monopoly, the rent would still be $300. That is well within my $658 budget.

p4 cannot build more houses on yellow because he only has $46 and each house costs $150. From space 2 I cannot reach yellow spaces in a single roll anyway.

p2 is currently on Pennsylvania Avenue.

p2 is 22 spaces away from Orange, so he cannot land there in one turn. p3 is on Park Place and also misses Orange on his next roll. Neither opponent can reach the Orange monopoly for at least two more turns.

I checked p4's possible landings from Water Works. He cannot reach Orange without drawing a Chance card. No opponent can land on Orange before my next turn.

I am now weighing whether to build the fourth house on Orange immediately. Four houses would raise rent by $200 per hit, but the $300 cost leaves only $358 cash. I am assessing the risks before those houses pay off.

I checked the exact Orange rent schedule. Three houses on each property yields $550–$600 per hit, and four houses raises it to $750–$800. The worst realistic landing is about $300, so the $358 cash buffer after building is sufficient. I also noted that p2 could still add a house to his red monopoly for $150, leaving him with roughly $49.

Red house costs are $150 each. p2 can only add one more house to his red monopoly for $150, leaving him with roughly $49. He cannot even the set to 2/2/2. Green properties are mortgaged and cannot be built on.

I checked the worst-case landing scenarios after building four houses. Income Tax costs $200, leaving $158. A Virginia 3-house hit or a Chance to Illinois both cost $300, leaving only $58. That is tight but survivable. I also noted that p2 cannot even his red set to 2/2/2 with his current cash.

The "Advance to Illinois" Chance card is one of sixteen, so the risk is low. The housing supply is not a concern: the bank has sixteen houses and twelve hotels remaining, and p3 cannot afford to buy all sixteen. Even if I build three more houses to reach four on each Orange property, the bank would still have thirteen houses left for p3 to use.

A fourth house on Orange would raise rent to $750–$800. p2 has only $199. Selling all four red houses yields $300, and mortgaging Boardwalk adds another $200. That still leaves him about $699 short of the rent. He would be bankrupt or nearly so if he lands on Orange with four houses.

Three houses on Orange leave p2 with roughly $149–$199 after selling his red houses and mortgaging Boardwalk, so he survives a $550–$600 hit. Four houses would bankrupt him with only about $51 left. p3 has enough cash and mortgageable properties to survive a $750–$800 hit, so four houses would not kill him.

Bankrupting p2 would hand me his red monopoly, Boardwalk, and mortgaged greens plus the railroad. That is a game-winning outcome.

I would hold both the Orange and Red monopolies. That is devastating.

p2 cannot reach Orange on his next roll. He must wait for his second turn after p3 and p4 finish. By then he will still be near the bottom of the board. He cannot land on Orange until his third turn.

p2 can reach Orange on his third turn, after p3 and p4 finish. Building now sets the trap immediately, though it leaves only $358 cash. That buffer covers the worst-case $300 rent from p3's Virginia 3-house hit.

I am now calculating the exact cash impact of Chance and Community Chest cards. "General repairs" costs $25 per house, so nine houses would cost $225. "Street repairs" costs $40 per house, which would be $360 with nine houses. I have not yet drawn these cards, but they could drain my remaining buffer.

I cannot land on Community Chest from space 2, so that card is not an immediate risk. The only nearby Chance card is "General repairs," which costs $25 per house. With nine houses that is $225, leaving me with $433 cash; with twelve houses it is $300, leaving me with $58. That $58 buffer is enough to survive. I also noted the "chairman" card costs $150. Building to four houses on Orange is the right move because the bankruptcy trap against p2 is the strategic prize.

I am now weighing a compromise: building only two more houses to keep New York at three while the others reach four. That would cost $200 and leave $458 cash, satisfying the one-house difference rule. New York has the highest rent at three houses, so leaving it there would reduce the worst-case hit from $750 to $600. p2 could survive a $600 rent but would still be bankrupted by a $750 hit.

I decided to build four houses on all three Orange properties. p2 could land on any of them, so the set must be fully maxed out to guarantee bankruptcy. The cost is $300 and leaves $358 cash. I also noted that Short Line unmortgaging would cost $110.

Unmortgaging Short Line is not worthwhile. The $110 cost would drain my cash buffer, and the lone railroad rent is only $25.

I considered trading with p3 or p4. I cannot acquire red properties from p2 because he holds all three. Park Place from p4 would be useless without Boardwalk. p4 has only $46 and little to offer.

I will not trade away houses or orange deeds.

I could trade now and build later, since the engine will ask again if actions remain. p3 has both light blue and pink monopolies with $705 cash and no houses yet, making them the biggest long-term threat. Breaking their monopolies would require a trade, but they would not give up a piece cheaply.

I will not give p2 cash. I considered buying p4's yellow monopoly to break it, but that would cost money and prevent me from building the fourth houses on Orange.
